outcomes: A person reads the runs, jobs and logs of Putnami CI, GitHub Actions and GitLab CI with the same putnami cloud ci commands, signed in, from a Putnami workspace or from a repository that has none, and sees why a run failed
nonGoals: Starting, cancelling or rerunning a pipeline of another CI: the reads change nothing
Artifacts, and the steps of a job that did not fail
A call to GitHub or GitLab from the CLI: Delivery reads them, and the CLI branches on no CI
Opening the log of a job to a delegated or machine session: Delivery decides who reads it

text: putnami cloud ci list --commit <revision> or --change <number> prints the pipelines of each CI in the same columns, with the reference the other commands take; structured output prints one pipeline per line, every member kept.
--commit takes any revision Git resolves; the repository is --repo, else the origin remote's, with a GitLab project's full group path.
Without both flags, list keeps reading the workspace's hosted runs.
putnami cloud ci providers prints each CI's state, and the reason when Cloud cannot read it.
A list that finds no pipeline prints those states too, so a CI that Cloud may not read does not look like a commit with no CI.
putnami cloud ci view --pipeline <ref> prints the jobs, failed ones first, then the failed steps and kept log excerpt of at most five jobs that fail the pipeline, and how many it left out.
A job allowed to fail or retried does not fail it; an excerpt that is missing is said with its reason.
--job selects one job by reference, id or name and refuses a name jobs share.
Structured output carries the pipeline, capabilities and failures, or the one job.
putnami cloud ci logs --pipeline <ref> prints the log of the job --job selects, else of the only failed job, else of the only job; otherwise it lists the jobs and refuses.
It says on stderr when it got the end of the log only, and names a refused or unreadable log with the job's page.
Text drops terminal control sequences, --raw keeps them, structured output prints one line per object; other run flags are refused.

list --commit or --change, providers, view --pipeline and logs --pipeline run in a repository with no Putnami workspace: --workspace names the Cloud workspace, and the control plane is the default one unless a flag or the environment names another.
With no link and no --workspace, the command refuses before any read and names --workspace.
